weakest_line: And if you're here to stand for God's word, welcome to the Valiant.
one_fix: Open on the concrete puzzle instead of the abstract question: Israel watched the sea split and heard God at Sinai, then built a golden calf within weeks. Then trim the philosopher name-drops so the Exodus evidence carries the answer.

weakest_line: So, let's allow the Bible to answer it.
one_fix: Cut the three-answer list down to Cornelius as the single proof (a man who never heard, and God sent the gospel to his door). End on a question a non-believer could answer too, instead of assuming the viewer was told about Jesus by someone.
Drop the colleague-lies analogy and use that time on the Peter vs Judas contrast (both failed that night, only one came back). That is the real payoff and it sets up the closing question.

weakest_line: Work in that world would feel like tending something you love.
one_fix: Replace speculation with text: anchor each change in a Genesis detail viewers miss (for example the tree of life and why access to it was cut off), so the answer is earned rather than imagined.

weakest_line: So the next time someone asks you where Cain's wife came from, you'll know what to say.
one_fix: Replace the flat closing line with an ending that lands on the 'one blood, one family' idea and invites a real response, such as a question about the discomfort viewers feel with the answer.
Lead with the textual puzzle instead of a sermon to 'we': why would an all-knowing God ask Adam 'Where art thou?' Then drop the assumptions about the viewer skipping church and avoiding their Bible.

weakest_line: So what is the unforgivable sin?
one_fix: Sharpen the hook into a specific puzzle (Jesus said one sin will never be forgiven, and he said it to men who had just watched him heal a blind, mute man). Simplify the dense middle so the Mark 3 'unclean spirit' explanation lands as the clear payoff.

weakest_line: Because it was the only thing standing between a family and death.
one_fix: Actually answer the hook: cut the Moses backstory and show from Exodus 12 why blood (a lamb dying in the firstborn's place, 'when I see the blood, I will pass over you') instead of a circular answer and a channel plug.

weakest_line: Some Christians also wonder about this question sometimes.
one_fix: Drop the muddled First/Second/Then/Third list and deal directly with the hardest part of the hook (why 'forever'), using one specific text, rather than stringing familiar invitation verses together.

weakest_line: So God gave us free will, and He tells us plainly which way to choose.
one_fix: Ground the answer in Genesis instead of hypotheticals. For example, show that the tree of life stood in the garden too and that God gave a clear command and warning, so the free-choice point is shown from the text rather than argued.
